intro: Lesson 15: 1.6 Social and economic justice in the Prophet's ﷺ teaching and example. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: What is justice?
points: Stand for justice even against yourselves (4:135)
Be just even with those you dislike (5:8)
Messengers were sent so people uphold justice (57:25)

passage.title: Bukhari and Muslim (meaning)
paras: Those before you were destroyed because when a noble person stole they left him, and when a weak person stole they punished him. By Allah, if Fatimah the daughter of Muhammad stole, I would cut off her hand.

panels.title: Care for the weak
points: Workers: 'they are your brothers' (Bukhari and Muslim)
Pay the worker his wage promptly (Ibn Majah)
Oppression is darkness on the Day of Judgement

head: Situation
The injustice
The Prophet's ﷺ teaching
Evidence
rows: A rich person steals and is let off

blocks.answers: Unpaid worker: pay the worker his wage promptly (Ibn Majah); workers are 'your brothers'. Rich thief: equality before the law, the Makhzumi woman (Bukhari and Muslim, meaning). Orphan's property: do not oppress the orphan (93:9; 4:10). Short measures: woe to those who give short measure (83:1-3). Together: a society built on 'adl, care for the weak and fair trade.

questions.q: Explain how the Prophet's ﷺ example promoted justice in society.
questions.a: 1) Same law for all: the Makhzumi woman. 2) Wealth for the poor: zakah and the ban on riba. Each with explanation and link to Muslim belief about society.

questions.q: Which ayah says 'Allah has permitted trade and forbidden riba'?

Table task then paragraph (portal response box): for four situations (unpaid worker, rich thief, orphan's property, short measures) give the injustice, the Prophet's ﷺ teaching and the evidence. Then explain what these show about Muslim beliefs about society.
questions.a: Correct teaching and evidence for each (wage hadith, Makhzumi, 93:9 or 4:10, 83:1-3); conclusion: society built on 'adl, care for the weak and accountability.

questions.q: Extend: why is riba seen as an economic injustice?
questions.a: It makes money grow from others' need without shared risk, concentrating wealth (59:7, 2:275).

questions.q: Stretch: does the Prophet's ﷺ rule of equality apply in a British court? Give a reason.
questions.a: Yes in principle: the rule of law means everyone is equal before it, matching the Makhzumi hadith.

questions.q: Which teaching is about ECONOMIC justice?
options: Wealth must not circulate only among the rich (59:7)
The noble and weak face the same law
Be just to those you dislike (5:8)
questions.a: A) Wealth must not circulate only among the rich (59:7). 59:7 is about the flow of wealth. The others are about justice in law and relationships.

questions.q: Think again: is a society fair if the powerful escape the law?
questions.a: No: justice means the same law for everyone.
